chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave his sheep to another man in exchange for clarified butter and a known amount of dirhams, so much and so much for each sheep every month. He said, 'There is no objection to the dirhams, but as for the clarified butter, I do not like that unless they are milking sheep, then there is no objection.'

key_terms.حَوَالِبَ: Milking animals (specifically those producing milk for the butter)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging livestock for butter and money in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between fixed monetary compensation and variable produce in a livestock contract, permitting the dirhams but expressing reservation regarding butter unless the animals are specifically designated as milking stock (*hawalib*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) in the quantity or quality of non-standardized goods, while allowing flexibility when the asset's primary utility (milk production) is clearly defined. The distinction underscores the importance of specifying the functional purpose of the livestock to ensure the validity of the exchange.
